StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeAttack.rationale: USES THE RIGHT SLOT, which is worth recording loudly: hooks.py has before_attack/after_attack slots that power/thorns, power/curl_up and power/skittish all fail to use (the main report's section 4 items 2, 5 and 14), and this power and power/vigor are the two that do. C#'s BeforeAttack takes an AttackCommand and latches the first one that qualifies; combat.py:479 fires before_attack once per play-count iteration around the card's on_play, which is the sim's attack-command boundary (stated at combat.py:472-475). All four C# guards are present: ModelSource is a CardModel (GigantificationPower.cs:30-33 vs powers.py:3965 `card is None`), the owner (:34-37 vs :3963), Type == Attack (:38-41 vs :3965), IsPoweredAttack (:42-45 vs :3965 card.is_unpowered), and the already-latched early return (:47-50 vs :3963).

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: 3 for the latched card, 3 for any powered card attack of the owner while nothing is latched (which is what makes the card's damage PREVIEW read triple, and the sim's docstring at powers.py:3940-3942 says so), 1 otherwise. GigantificationPower.cs:57-74 vs powers.py:3979-3983: cardSource == null, the owner, IsPoweredAttack (structural via cmds.py:56-58) and the commandToModify-vs-cardSource comparison all line up, with the sim comparing CARD identity where C# compares command.ModelSource -- the same object for a card attack. The literal 3 at GigantificationPower.cs:72 matches powers.py:3949's MULTIPLIER = 3, and 3 is dyadic-safe as an integer factor (executed: py audit/tools/power_census.py multipliers lists it among the safe ones), so this power does not widen hook_dispatch's G9.

AfterAttack.issue: The slot is right (combat.py:492, immediately after the card's on_play inside the play-count loop). The GAP is the IDENTITY the latch is cleared against: C# compares ATTACK-COMMAND identity (`command == internalData.commandToModify`, GigantificationPower.cs:80), the sim compares CARD identity (`card is self._card_to_modify`, powers.py:3986). They agree for one card producing one attack command, which is the normal case. They diverge when ONE card produces SEVERAL attack commands -- C# clears and Decrements once per matching command, i.e. once, while the sim clears and _ticks on the first after_attack for that card and then, because the latch is now None, the NEXT hit of the same card re-enters modify_damage_multiplicative on the `_card_to_modify is None` arm (powers.py:3981) and gets tripled AGAIN for free. DORMANT: combat.py:477-494 fires exactly one before_attack/after_attack pair per play-count iteration and a multi-hit card resolves inside one iteration, so no ported card reaches the second command. Named trigger: any card or effect that issues two attack commands within one play, or a port that moves before_attack/after_attack inside a card's own hit loop.

guards.rationale: powers.py:3951-3959 initialises self._card_to_modify in __init__, which is the sim's equivalent of InitInternalData. Note this power is NOT PowerInstanceType.Instanced (unlike power/automation, power/the_bomb, power/rolling_boulder and power/toric_toughness), so one shared latch per owner is correct on both sides and power_cmd's G5 does not apply here.

guards.what: GigantificationPower.cs:83 PowerCmd.Decrement, once per triggered attack
guards.rationale: powers.py:3988 self._tick(). So Gigantification 2 triples two separate Attack cards, not one card twice. The sim's Power._tick (powers.py:70-75) decrements the field and _expires at <= 0 where C# routes through PowerCmd.Decrement -> ModifyAmount -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount (PowerCmd.cs:215-250); PowerCmd.Decrement, NOT TickDownDuration, so neither side honours SkipNextDurationTick. Observationally identical -- ModifyAmount's only unconditional modifier leg is Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived (PowerCmd.cs:234), whose ported listeners are ArtifactPower (Debuff-only) and RuinedHelmet (StrengthPower-only). Same mechanism and same verdict as audits/power/colossus.json's AfterSideTurnEnd guard, per binding rule 3.

guards.what: GigantificationPower.cs:77-85 AfterAttack has NO owner guard
guards.rationale: C# relies on the command comparison alone; powers.py:3986 relies on the card comparison alone. Equivalent -- neither can match another creature's attack, because the latch was only ever set for the owner's own card.

guards.what: The applier is a potion, and the potion KIND has no audit tier
guards.rationale: NARROWED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass). The old rationale said "what is waived is only the REACHABILITY of its one applier". That was wrong twice over: it is logically incompatible with this record tagging any hook LIVE (LIVE is itself a reachability claim), and it is stale -- Gigantification Potion is ported and POOL-REGISTERED, so the power is reachable in the sim today whether or not the potion tier is ever written. What is genuinely out of scope, and all this waiver now claims, is the potion UNIT's own record: potions are a deferred kind by Perry's deferral (the shared audit contract's Global scope section) and there is no audit/records/potion/ tier for Gigantification Potion to live in, so nothing here judges the potion's own fidelity (cost, targeting, belt behaviour). REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED, not waived: the sim ports the potion at potions.py:802-819, @register_potion puts it in ALL_POTIONS, and it is in the generation pool at potion_pools.py:53 (rare). The POWER is audited in full above and every liveness label on this record stands on its own evidence. Same correction at all seven power records carrying this guard (power/buffer, power/clarity, power/flex_potion, power/gigantification, power/radiance, power/shackling_potion, power/speed_potion) so the mechanism keeps one verdict at every site per binding rule 3.
